identity: A chapter from an Arabic scholarly-popular book on the history of money: title أصل النقود وبدء ضربها, running section headings معاملات الإنسان الأول and السلع النقدية, and expository body prose between them. Early/mid-20th-century Egyptian learned register — periodic sentences, elevated diction, transliterated technical terms (الباليوليطيقي، النيوليطيقي), and authorities marshalled in series (آدم سميث، ابن خلدون، الأستاذ زيمل، المقريزي، إلياذة هوميروس). This is my doctrine's §L/§B register: encyclopedic/expository nonfiction, the longest-unit family in the corpus (25-45 tokens), and the register in which batch 2 caught me over-cutting 2-3x.
law: The unit is the printed full stop of a periodic expository sentence, running 25-45 tokens. Every <NL> is preceded by a boundary and each heading is its own segment. Inside a paragraph, cut ONLY where the source must have carried an end-stop: a completed reported thesis followed by full re-nomination of its subject; an interrogative that cannot subordinate to the preceding declarative; an anaphoric demonstrative (زعمهم هذا، وهذا هو) that points back at an already-closed proposition; or a summarising predication that shuts an أن-complement chain. Connectives are never boundaries in this register: و، ف، ثم، حتى، كما، حيث، حين، إلا أن، ولكن، ولذلك، وهي، فقد all weld, as do relative clauses, comma-lists, appositions and exemplification strings.
reasoning: Register first (LAW 6), then segment. Headings plus periodic prose citing named authorities puts this squarely in §L/§B, so the operating posture is LAW 0-double-prime: default WELD, cut only at a nameable mark. Free boundaries: 12 <NL> plus the final token = 13, taken without argument (confirmed prior, 100% over 41 docs). Seven internal cuts, argued. (1) @122 الحيوان: يقول الاقتصادي الكبير آدم سميث ... إن الإنسان مدفوع بسليقته is a complete reported thesis and G1 keeps a speech verb with its whole quotation; the next clause opens ولكن آدم سميث لم يبين لنا, re-nominating the proper name in full instead of pronominalising it, which is a printed-sentence signal rather than a bare ولكن — B4 requires a preceding stop and this is it. (2) @205 عنه: كيف opens an interrogative that cannot be subordinate to the preceding declarative, and it is a complete rhetorical turn closing the section (T8). (3) @233 صاحبه: إن التعامل ... is the paragraph-initial thesis about WHO traded; ولم تكن الحاجيات shifts topic to WHAT was traded. I took 233 over the rival site 243 because ولما كانت اللحوم ... فإن الجلود والعظام is anaphorically welded to the list اللحوم والجلود والعظام immediately preceding it, and a stop at 243 would break that pair; حتى قال المؤرخون is consecutive and cannot open a sentence, so it welds backward. (4) @280 الأرزاق: زعمهم هذا refers back to the historians' claim as a finished object — one calls something this claim of theirs only after it has closed. (5) @324 تتداول: وصح بذلك رأي المقريزي is the conclusion drawn from the excavation evidence, and I placed the stop before وصح rather than before فقد because LAW 4 keeps a trailing فقد justification attached to its main clause (the identical shape recurs at @538, where I weld). (6) @367 وأحجامها and (7) @559 ثيران are the same construction twice — وهذا هو plus a summarising demonstrative that shuts an أن-complement block and pivots to a new authority / to the modern parallel. These are correlated bets so I judged them together: cutting both yields 43/19 and 28/25, all inside the band, whereas welding both yields 62 and 53, both outside it. Sites deliberately WELDED against instinct: @136 فلم and @151 ولم (coordinated negated verbs under one subject — LAW 1 and LAW 2, a connective is never a reason); @159 زيمل (حين قال is grammatically bound to مذهب الأستاذ زيمل — B2); @187 والحرمان (وهي appositive continuation, which §N and §L both record as a confirmed false cut of mine); @257 المعاملات (حتى consecutive); @303 العصور (ويستنتجون merely coordinates with ويستندون, tight anaphora on هذه العظام والمحار); @342 and @360 (وأنه and ويفرق sit inside the ثبت complement); @409 الإنسانية (إلا أن is the apodosis of وإن كنا — B3); @429 and @442 (relative clauses on النيوليطيقي, and ثم inside one); @467 and @474 (the وبديهي / ولا شك / ومن المحقق tricolon — LAW 3, parallelism is dead as a cut criterion); @485 (وهي plus a four-item apposition list); @513 ولذلك (§N result connective welds); @523 (coordinated PP pair inside one balance-scale image); @538 فقد, @550 كما, @571 حيث (all named weld-triggers in B2 and T4); @605 (coordinated كـ exemplification). Two segments come out long — 123-205 at 83 tokens and 391-451 at 61. I accepted both deliberately: every internal candidate inside them is exactly a move my doctrine records as producing false cuts and zero misses in batch 2 (و-coordination, وهي, حين, إلا أن, relative clauses), and LAW 0 as revised forbids letting a token count override the absence of a nameable mark. Sanity check on the swing (item 9): 20 boundaries over 603 real tokens is one per 30, and the mean prose segment is 35 tokens — centred in the §L band, so the two long segments are a local anomaly, not a global under-cutting posture. T6 log: the paragraph-initial وقد at @494 is consistent with وقد marking a fresh assertion, though paragraph position makes it non-diagnostic here.
